canonical_truth.summary: The fox who has held the rocky shoulder above the brook for as many winters as YY can count has moved on. Her scent-mark on the old scratch-pine has gone cold; her trail leads away over the ridge and does not return. A wedge of woods that has been functionally off-limits to small foragers is suddenly available. The rocky shoulder is one of the better forage zones in early spring — it holds last fall's stranded mast in its crevices and gets warm soil before anywhere else.
canonical_truth.location: the rocky shoulder above the north bank of the brook, the slope marked by the old scratch-pine
canonical_truth.concrete_outcome: A long-held territorial boundary lifts. Small foragers who would never have crossed the scratch-pine line are suddenly free to. The fox's exit trail is fresh enough to read.

perception_prompt.noticeable_surface: The smell that has always been at the scratch-pine — sharp, slightly sweet, old-fox — is not there this morning. The pine itself looks the same; the air around it does not.

authorial_note.real_world_inspiration: Indian PM Narendra Modi's BJP won a key legislative election in West Bengal on 2026-05-05, ending fifteen years of rule by Mamata Banerjee — a long-held political boundary changing hands.
authorial_note.translation_logic: A long-stable territorial boundary ends. For YY this becomes the fox's scent-mark gone cold at the scratch-pine — a line he and every other small forager have respected for years, suddenly absent. The geopolitical handover translates to a sensory absence and a new wedge of forageable ground.
authorial_note.restraint_reason: The world enters as a smell that should be there and isn't. YY does not understand long rules; he understands the shape of a smell at a tree he has walked past every day, and he understands when it is missing.
